html:
A university in Lima, founded by a royal decree of Charles V on 12 May 1551. It is the oldest officially established university in the Americas and has operated ever since.

It grew out of studies held by Dominican friars in their convent. Like Spanish universities such as Salamanca, it taught theology, law, arts and later medicine. Its graduates staffed the church and the government of the Viceroyalty of Peru, which ruled most of Spanish South America. Teaching of Quechua was added so priests could preach in the language of the Andes.

A rival claim to "first university" belongs to Santo Domingo, whose university dates from a papal bull of 1538, and the Royal University of Mexico was founded by decree a few months after San Marcos. In the 1800s and 1900s San Marcos was the home of Peruvian politics and thought, and many of the country's presidents and writers studied there.
sum: A university in Lima, founded by a royal decree of Charles V on 12 May 1551. It is the oldest officially established university in the Americas and has operated ever since.
